articles.title: Sound Waves Help Chemo Reach Brain Tumours, Extending Survival by 40 Percent
articles.excerpt: A landmark trial shows focused ultrasound can safely open the blood-brain barrier, delivering more chemotherapy to glioblastoma and boosting survival from 19 to 31 months.
articles.nri_angle: Glioblastoma affects over 28,000 Indians annually, and global trials including centres in Asia could accelerate access to the treatment for patients in India and the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Glyphosate Exposure During Mid-Pregnancy Linked to Preterm Birth Risk
articles.excerpt: An NYU Langone study of 1,450 women found that higher levels of the common weedkiller Roundup's active ingredient during midpregnancy raised the odds of spontaneous early labor.
articles.nri_angle: Glyphosate is the second most consumed herbicide in India, widely used beyond its approved scope, and Indian diaspora families face exposure through both the U.S. and Indian food supplies.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Free HPV Vaccination Drive Crosses Five Months With Strong Uptake
articles.excerpt: The nationwide campaign launched in February has vaccinated millions of 14-year-old girls across all states, with Karnataka among the states reporting surging demand at government health centres.
articles.image_caption: India's free HPV vaccination program, which began in February 2026, has seen strong uptake among girls aged 9–14 across all states and union territories.
articles.nri_angle: India's free HPV drive brings the same cervical cancer prevention long standard in the US, UK, and Australia to families in India, including those with diaspora connections.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hardik Pandya Sports Tonsured Head During Tirumala Temple Visit with Girlfriend Mahieka Sharma
articles.excerpt: The Indian cricket star was photographed with a shaved head alongside his model girlfriend at the Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple, sparking fresh discussion about the couple's deepening spiritual bond.
articles.image_caption: Indian all-rounder Hardik Pandya, who was spotted visiting the Tirumala temple with a tonsured head alongside girlfriend Mahieka Sharma.
articles.nri_angle: Pandya's public tonsure ritual at Tirumala resonates with diaspora Indians maintaining spiritual connections to Hindu pilgrimage traditions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: FDA Advisory Panel Backs Six Peptides for Pharmacy Compounding Despite Safety Concerns
articles.excerpt: In a win for RFK Jr. and the wellness industry, advisers voted 8-6 to recommend broader access to injectable peptides like BPC-157 and TB-500, overriding FDA staff objections over limited human safety data.
articles.nri_angle: India's peptide API manufacturing sector and Indian-American telehealth entrepreneurs stand to benefit from a broadened U.S. compounding market worth up to $3 billion.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Novo Nordisk's $725 Million Bet on Heart Inflammation Drug Fails in Major Trial
articles.excerpt: Ziltivekimab did not reduce cardiovascular events in a 6,300-patient Phase 3 trial, sending shares down 9% and raising questions about the pharma giant's pipeline beyond obesity drugs.
articles.image_caption: Novo Nordisk's experimental heart inflammation drug monlunabant failed to meet its primary endpoint in a major Phase 3 trial.
articles.nri_angle: The ZEUS trial failure highlights the challenges even large pharma companies face in developing cardiovascular drugs, an area of acute relevance for South Asians who face elevated heart disease risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Viagra May Slow Cancer Spread by Blocking Tumour Cholesterol, Major Study Finds
articles.excerpt: Israeli researchers report that sildenafil disrupts a key cholesterol pathway cancer cells use to metastasise, with better survival seen in a 40,000-patient analysis.
articles.nri_angle: Major medical research finding relevant to global health discussions, with potential implications for cancer treatment protocols worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: After 'Ozempic Face,' Experts Now Warn of 'Ozempic Hair' Side Effect
articles.excerpt: A major BMJ study links GLP-1 weight-loss drugs to a 37–68% higher risk of hair loss, adding to a growing list of aesthetic side effects reported by millions of users.
articles.nri_angle: GLP-1 drugs are increasingly popular among Indian Americans, making awareness of side effects like hair loss particularly relevant for the diaspora community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: WHO Says 45% of Dementia Cases Preventable, Adds Air Pollution as Risk Factor
articles.excerpt: Updated guidelines identify 19 modifiable risk factors and advise against routine supplements, with particular urgency for India's 8.8 million dementia patients and its pollution crisis.
articles.image_caption: WHO's updated guidelines identify 17 modifiable risk factors for dementia, including air pollution, now deemed preventable in 45% of cases
articles.nri_angle: With 8.8 million Indians aged 60+ affected, the guidelines urge diaspora families to prioritize prevention for aging parents, especially given India's severe air pollution burden.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kerala Monsoon Death Toll Climbs to Six as Floods and Landslips Ravage Kottayam
articles.excerpt: Heavy rainfall has triggered landslips and caused rivers to overflow across Kerala's Kottayam district, killing at least six people as the India Meteorological Department warns of continued downpours.
articles.nri_angle: Keralites abroad, one of India's largest diaspora communities, closely monitor monsoon conditions given family members and property in flood-prone areas.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Broad Peak Avalanche Kills Four, Nirmal Purja Among Six Still Missing
articles.excerpt: A devastating avalanche on Pakistan's 12th-highest peak swept away 10 climbers from four expeditions, including American Mallory Geis who had left her Pilates career to pursue mountaineering.
articles.nri_angle: The avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak, in the Karakoram range of Gilgit-Baltistan, killed Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi and disrupted a region central to Pakistan's growing mountaineering tourism industry.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Strong El Niño to Intensify From August, Adding Fuel to 'a Planet Already on Fire'
articles.excerpt: The World Meteorological Organization warns El Niño will steadily strengthen through October, combining with a positive Indian Ocean Dipole to amplify drought, floods, and heatwave risks worldwide.
articles.nri_angle: India faces its weakest monsoon in 11 years as El Niño suppresses rainfall, threatening food prices, crop exports, and inflation — key concerns for the Indian diaspora watching economic conditions back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gujarat Lung Cancer Cases Surge as State's Tobacco Acreage Keeps Expanding
articles.excerpt: GCRI treated 55% more lung cancer patients in 2024 than in 2020, while Gujarat's tobacco cultivation area grew 20% to over 200,000 hectares despite the Centre's crop diversification push.
articles.nri_angle: NRGs and overseas patients increasingly travel to Gujarat for affordable, advanced cancer treatment at GCRI and other state hospitals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Coral Reef Presumed Dead for 60 Years Rediscovered Alive and Thriving Off the Coast of Benin
articles.excerpt: Underwater drones deployed by Beninese scientists found a deep-water coral ecosystem teeming with life in the Gulf of Guinea, more than six decades after surveys dismissed it as a dead formation.
articles.nri_angle: India has its own understudied mesophotic reef systems along the Lakshadweep and Andaman coasts that could benefit from similar exploration efforts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chemicals in Chlorinated Drinking Water Linked to Increased Risk of Uterine Cancer, Major Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A 25-year study tracking more than 53,000 California women found that common disinfection byproducts in tap water, including trihalomethanes and haloacetic acids, are associated with significantly elevated uterine cancer risk.
articles.nri_angle: Chlorination remains the dominant water treatment method in most Indian cities, where DBP monitoring is far less rigorous than in the U.S.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's New LPG Rules Mandate OTP Verification and Slash Subsidized Cylinders
articles.excerpt: The central government's overhaul of cooking gas distribution requires Aadhaar-linked e-KYC, OTP-based delivery authentication, and cuts subsidized cylinders from nine to four per year under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs maintaining LPG connections for family in India should ensure relatives complete mandatory e-KYC verification to avoid losing cooking gas subsidies.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Breakthrough HIV Prevention Drug Could Slash Infections, but Funding Cuts Block Access
articles.excerpt: Lenacapavir, a twice-yearly injection with near-perfect efficacy, is reaching only a fraction of those who need it as USAID and global donor pullbacks cripple distribution.
articles.nri_angle: Indian American physicians and global health researchers are at the forefront of lenacapavir advocacy, while Indian generic manufacturers hold the key to making the drug affordable worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rare Gene Mutations Can Trigger Atrial Fibrillation Decades Before Typical Onset
articles.excerpt: Large-scale genomic studies reveal that single inherited gene variants, not common polygenic risk, drive irregular heartbeats in younger patients — raising questions about when genetic testing should begin.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated cardiovascular risk, and genetic testing for early-onset AFib could help identify at-risk individuals in the diaspora before complications develop.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Merck-Wellcome Venture Tapped to Manufacture WHO's Top Bundibugyo Ebola Vaccine
articles.excerpt: Hilleman Laboratories will produce clinical trial doses of IAVI's single-dose vaccine with $8.5 million in CEPI funding, as Congo's Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak surpasses 3,300 cases.
articles.nri_angle: India's Serum Institute is manufacturing a rival Oxford-developed Bundibugyo vaccine candidate, and Hilleman Laboratories — originally founded in India before relocating to Singapore — draws on deep ties to South Asian pharmaceutical infrastructure.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Menopause Before 40 Raises Heart Disease Risk by 40 Percent, Major Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A JAMA Cardiology study of over 10,000 women links premature menopause to sharply elevated cardiovascular risk, with blood pressure, cholesterol, and body composition all shifting unfavorably.
articles.nri_angle: Women in the Indian diaspora, who may already face higher cardiovascular risk due to genetic predisposition and lifestyle factors, should include menopause timing in their heart-health conversations with doctors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Medicaid Work Requirements Set to Strip Coverage From Millions as US Hospitals Sound the Alarm
articles.excerpt: As the One Big Beautiful Bill Act's 'community engagement requirements' approach their January 2027 deadline, hospitals are already reeling from a surge in uninsured patients — and the worst is yet to come.
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans on Medicaid expansion — particularly small business workers, gig economy participants, and recent immigrants — face new documentation burdens and potential coverage loss under work requirements, with heightened risk given higher rates of chronic conditions like diabetes in the community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mosquitoes Can Learn to Love DEET, Turning Bug Spray Into a Dinner Bell
articles.excerpt: A new study shows lab mosquitoes trained to associate the world's most popular repellent with blood meals began actively seeking out DEET-treated skin — a finding with implications for tropical disease prevention worldwide.
articles.nri_angle: DEET-based repellents are a primary defence for diaspora members travelling to India during monsoon season, when dengue and malaria transmission peaks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Surgeon at University of Maryland Removes Rare Spinal Tumour Through Patient's Eye Socket in World First
articles.excerpt: Dr. Mohamed Labib led a team that removed a chordoma from a 19-year-old's spine via a transorbital approach, while a separate brain tumour was extracted through her nose — both firsts in neurosurgical technique.
articles.image_caption: University of Maryland Medical Center, where Dr. Narendra Nath Jha performed the world's first transorbital spinal tumour removal.
articles.nri_angle: Endoscopic neurosurgery techniques pioneered by teams like Dr. Labib's are increasingly adopted at Indian medical centres, expanding minimally invasive options.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Akshar Yoga Kendraa Sets 21 Guinness World Records on International Yoga Day
articles.excerpt: Over 10,000 participants from more than 100 countries gathered in Bengaluru for what became one of the largest coordinated yoga record attempts in history.
articles.nri_angle: Yoga remains one of the strongest cultural connectors for the Indian diaspora, with record events reinforcing India's global yoga leadership.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Lung Cancer Surges Among Young Non-Smoking Women in India
articles.excerpt: Non-smoking women in their 40s now account for up to 40 percent of female lung cancer cases in India, driven by air pollution, indoor cooking fumes, and genetic mutations — while screening protocols still focus on older male smokers.
articles.nri_angle: EGFR mutations prevalent in Asian populations make genetic risk factors relevant for Indian diaspora families, while air quality and indoor cooking exposure during visits to India compound the concern.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cancers Once Diagnosed at 60 Are Now Striking People in Their 30s and 40s, and Researchers Think They Know Why
articles.excerpt: A landmark Nature Medicine study links accelerated biological aging in younger generations to the global surge in early-onset cancers, with implications for how we screen and prevent the disease.
articles.nri_angle: India faces rising early-onset cancer rates; South Asians in Western countries show elevated risk for certain cancers in younger age groups.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi High Court Refuses to Halt India's HPV Vaccination Drive, Seeks Centre's Response on Safety Concerns
articles.excerpt: The court declined a stay on the national immunisation programme but called the issue 'very important' and ordered responses from ICMR, CDSCO, and NITAG.
articles.nri_angle: HPV vaccination is standard in Western countries where most NRIs live; India's rollout and safety debate directly affects families with children in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: GLP-1 Weight Loss Drugs Linked to Sharply Lower Risk of Obesity-Related Cancers, Studies Show
articles.excerpt: Multiple large-scale studies suggest medications like Ozempic and Mounjaro may reduce cancer risk by up to 65 percent for some tumour types, with researchers now investigating mechanisms beyond weight loss.
articles.nri_angle: With obesity and diabetes rates rising sharply among South Asians, GLP-1 drugs' potential anti-cancer benefits carry particular relevance for the Indian diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cambridge Study Reveals Why Some Smokers Get Cancer and Others Do Not
articles.excerpt: A landmark Nature study finds that inherited genetics — not just environmental exposure — shapes how tumours evolve after DNA damage, offering the first direct evidence for a long-suspected link.
articles.image_caption: A Cambridge study found that certain DNA repair mechanisms determine why some long-term smokers develop cancer while others do not.
articles.nri_angle: India has among the highest rates of tobacco-related cancers globally, and understanding population-specific genetic risk could lead to better-tailored screening for Indian communities worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Plant-Forward Planetary Health Diet Linked to 28 Percent Lower Heart Disease Risk in Women
articles.excerpt: A 20-year study of more than 65,000 postmenopausal women found that even moderate adherence to the EAT-Lancet diet — rich in vegetables, whole grains and legumes — was associated with significantly reduced cardiovascular risk.
articles.nri_angle: The Planetary Health Diet aligns closely with traditional Indian dietary patterns built around dal, vegetables and whole grains, providing scientific validation for long-standing culinary wisdom.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Dengue or Viral Fever? The Early Warning Signs Doctors Want You to Know
articles.excerpt: As India's monsoon season drives a surge in dengue cases, medical experts explain how to distinguish the mosquito-borne disease from common viral fever before complications develop.
articles.image_caption: The Aedes aegypti mosquito, the primary carrier of the dengue virus. Health authorities urge early testing to distinguish dengue from common viral fevers.
articles.nri_angle: Indians traveling to India during monsoon season or with family in endemic areas need to recognize dengue symptoms early and inform doctors about travel history for prompt testing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Young Women Fuel Sharp Rise in Type 2 Diabetes Across England, Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A landmark Imperial College London analysis reveals early-onset type 2 diabetes diagnoses are surging among women under 40, driven by escalating obesity rates in younger generations.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin researcher Dr. Shivani Misra led the study, and South Asians remain disproportionately affected by early-onset type 2 diabetes, developing it at lower body weights than other ethnic groups.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Millions of Indians Live With Hepatitis B Without Knowing It as World Pushes to Break Down Barriers to Care
articles.excerpt: Ahead of World Hepatitis Day on July 28, global health bodies and Indian experts are urging aggressive screening and treatment to reach the estimated 40 million carriers who remain undiagnosed.
articles.nri_angle: Indian diaspora members with family in India should be aware of the massive undiagnosed hepatitis B burden and encourage screening during visits home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Records Nearly 560 New Oral Cancer Cases Every Day, Doctors Push for Simple Mirror Test
articles.excerpt: With one-third of the global oral cancer burden, India's oncologists are urging a two-minute monthly self-exam that could catch the disease at its most treatable stage.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora families who maintain cultural practices like paan and supari face elevated oral cancer risk and may lack access to routine oral screenings abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
